title: spec span/colSpan tier prose is anchored to the current .objectui-sha and goes stale at the bump that absorbs objectui#9253 — nothing mechanical holds the ticket
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-16T17:10Z, out of the #17670 remediation round (PR #18492). ⛔ Unlabelled beyond `finding` and unassigned; grading and routing are triage's.

⭐ This is a **scheduled staleness**, not a defect on the tree today. Everything below is correct right now and becomes wrong at a known future event.

## What PR #18492 does, and why it is right

`FormField.colSpan` and `FormField.span` carried two claims that #17328 measured **false**. PR #18492 replaces them with text that states what each key **resolves to** — true on both renderer states — and then **anchors the tier behaviour to a named commit** rather than asserting it timelessly:

> at the `.objectui-sha` pin `53ded82bf7` only the widest tier's class is emitted (`@2xl:col-span-3` for a 3-column grid), so at intermediate widths the field rendered identically to omitting the key

That is the honest shape while the pin sits where it does. Measured at both states by executing the two renderer implementations:

| probe, 3-column grid | pin `53ded82bf7` | objectui `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `span: 'full'` | `@2xl:col-span-3` | `@md:col-span-2 @2xl:col-span-3` |
| `colSpan: 4` | `@2xl:col-span-3` | `@md:col-span-2 @2xl:col-span-3` |

The renderer-side fix is **objectui#9253**, commit `bd09957380` (2026-09-12), trailer 「Part of objectui#9244」. It is **unreleased** at this repo's pin (`@object-ui/components` 17.6.0 at both the pin and objectui main; **0** tags contain the commit).

## The edge

**At the `.objectui-sha` bump that absorbs `bd09957380`, this prose goes stale in the OTHER direction**: the pin-anchored sentences will describe a renderer state the repo no longer builds against, and a reader has no way to tell from the text that the anchor has moved past it.

⚠️ **Nothing mechanical enforces the re-read.** The PR's TSDoc says so **in place** —

> objectui#9253 (objectui `bd09957380`, ahead of that pin) emits one clamped class per multi-column tier … **re-read this block at the pin bump that absorbs it**

— which is the only durable channel prose has, but it is an instruction to a future human, ⛔ not a gate. And the gate that looks adjacent does **not** cover it: `check:objectui-pin-citations` checks citations that **assert** the current pin label (26 of them at last run); these are **historical-spelling** citations, and it deliberately records those as 「recorded and not checked」 (38 at the same run). ⇒ the one gate in the area is designed not to fire here.

## ⛔ Why this is not solved by 「just don't anchor to a pin」

The alternative is what PR #18492 is removing: a timeless assertion about renderer behaviour, which is exactly what went false. Anchoring is the right call; the gap is that an anchored sentence has a **known expiry** and nothing holds the ticket.

## Possible directions — ⛔ no ruling implied

1. Extend `check:objectui-pin-citations` so a **historical-spelling** citation whose sha becomes an ancestor of the new pin is reported at the bump — it already parses both spellings, so it has the inputs.
2. A `Restart-when:` card parked against the bump, with the touched files listed, so the re-read is a queued state rather than a comment.
3. Accept the in-place instruction as the guard and close this. ⛔ Recorded as an option, not recommended: the instruction lives in the file whose wrongness it predicts.

## ⚠️ Not measured

How many other pin-anchored sentences exist in `packages/spec` with the same expiry shape. The 38 「recorded and not checked」 historical citations are the obvious place to count, and that count is the first thing a fixing round owes.

## Dedupe words

`spanLadderFor` · `objectui#9253` · `span-full-tier-ladder` · `pin bump reconcile` · `objectui-pin-citations historical`

## Refs
